```{r}
# Install all the Packages needed

```

```{r}
#load concentration data with clean names
concentration_data <- clean_names(read.csv(here("data", "concentration_data.csv"))) #To read csv files in the file system here package has used and #Clean up the names of the columns according to tidydata principles
concentration_data

#loadbinary data (detect/non-detect)
binary_data <- clean_names(read.csv(here("data","binary_table.csv")))
binary_data
```

## Calculation of detection percentage

```{r}
# Filter binary data based on detection percentage
# Remove sample names and the sampleType column, then select sample columns for detect percentage calculation
binary_data_matrix <- binary_data[,-1]  # Since Sample IDs are in binary data one binary data

# Calculate detection percentages
detection_percentages <- colSums(binary_data_matrix) / nrow(binary_data_matrix) * 100
detection_percentages
write.csv(detection_percentages, "detection_percentages.csv")

# Select analytes with 10% or higher detection percentage
selected_analytes <- names(detection_percentages[detection_percentages >= 75])
selected_analytes
```
```{r}
# Filter concentration data to include only selected analytes
filtered_data <- concentration_data %>%
  select(all_of(c("sample", "species", "basin", selected_analytes)))
filtered_data
```


```{r}
# Apply log10 transformation directly to analyte columns
log_transformed_data <- filtered_data %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(selected_analytes), ~ log10(.x)))
log_transformed_data
```

```{r}
# Define analyte columns dynamically (i.e., all columns after column 3)
selected_analytes <- colnames(log_transformed_data)[4:ncol(log_transformed_data)]
selected_analytes

## Step 1: Reshape data to long format
long_data <- log_transformed_data %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = 4:ncol(.),                     # All analyte columns
    names_to = "analyte", 
    values_to = "value"
  )
long_data

# Step 2: Group by basin and analyte, but ensure sufficient valid data
anova_results <- long_data %>%
  group_by(basin, analyte) %>%
  nest() %>%
  mutate(
    valid = map_lgl(data, ~ {
      d <- .x
      has_multiple_species <- n_distinct(d$species) > 1
      has_valid_values <- all(is.finite(d$value), na.rm = TRUE)
      has_non_na <- sum(!is.na(d$value)) >= 2
      has_multiple_species && has_valid_values && has_non_na
    })
  ) %>%
  filter(valid) %>%
  mutate(
    anova_result = map(data, ~ aov(value ~ species, data = .x) %>% tidy())
  ) %>%
  unnest(anova_result) %>%
  filter(term == "species") %>%
  select(basin, analyte, p.value)

# Preview the result
head(anova_results)
anova_results
```

```{r}
# Step 4: Count how often each analyte has p > 0.05
low_var_analytes <- anova_results %>%
  mutate(non_significant = p.value > 0.05) %>%
  group_by(analyte) %>%
  summarise(non_sig_count = sum(non_significant)) %>%
  filter(non_sig_count >= 2)  # Keep analytes with low species variability in at least 2 basins

low_var_analytes
```

```{r}
# Step 1: Extract the analytes with low variance (from previous step)
selected_analytes_anova <- low_var_analytes$analyte
selected_analytes_anova

# Step 2: Filter original (non-log) concentration data
# Assume 'concentration_data' is your original data frame (non-log-transformed)
pca_input <- concentration_data %>%
  select(sample, species, basin, all_of(selected_analytes_anova))
pca_input
```

```{r}

# Assuming 'filtered_data' is a data frame with PAC concentrations from 4th column to the last column
# Calculate the total PAC concentration for each sample using columns 3 to last
concentration_filtered <- pca_input %>%
  rowwise() %>% #do the operations raw by raw individually
  mutate(Total_PAC = sum(c_across(4:last_col()))) # Take the summary of each raw
concentration_filtered

# Calculate the percent contribution of each analyte (in columns 4 to last) to the total HPAC concentration
percent_normalized_data <- concentration_filtered %>%
  mutate(across(4:last_col(), ~ (. / Total_PAC) * 100)) # ~ introduce the anonymous function to each column and . is representing each sample
percent_normalized_data

# Step 3: Drop the 'Total_PAC' column if not needed for PCA
percent_normalized_data <- percent_normalized_data %>%
  select(-sample, -species,-basin, -Total_PAC) # remove the column with total PACs concentration
percent_normalized_data # The 'percent_normalized_data' now contains the percent contribution HPACs profiles.

```




```{r}

# Perform PCA on the normalized percent concentration data
pca_results <- PCA(percent_normalized_data, graph = FALSE)

# Extract PCA results
pca_values <- as.data.frame(pca_results$ind$coord)
pca_values <- cbind(concentration_filtered[, c("sample", "species", "basin")], pca_values[, 1:3])
colnames(pca_values)[4:6] <- c("PC1", "PC2", "PC3")
pca_values

# Save PCA values in the output folder
write.csv(pca_values, here("output", "PCA_values_HPACs.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```

```{r}

# Identify high-loading analytes for each principal component
loading_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_results$var$coord)
high_loading_analytes <- lapply(1:3, function(i) {
  loading_scores %>%
    select(contains(paste0("Dim.", i))) %>%
    rownames_to_column(var = "sample") %>%
    arrange(desc(abs(get(paste0("Dim.", i))))) %>%
    head(5) %>%
    pull(sample)
})
names(high_loading_analytes) <- c("PC1_high", "PC2_high", "PC3_high")
loading_scores
high_loading_analytes

# Save loading scores to a CSV file
write.csv(high_loading_analytes, here("output", "high_loading_analytes_HPAC.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
```

```{r}

# Save loading scores to a CSV file
loading_scores <- as.data.frame(pca_results$var$coord)
write.csv(loading_scores, here("output", "PCA_loading_scores.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

# Save eigenvalues to a CSV file
eigenvalues <- as.data.frame(pca_results$eig)
write.csv(eigenvalues, here("output", "PCA_eigenvalues.csv"), row.names = TRUE)

```



```{r}
# Plot PCA results with different colors for each basin and shapes for each species (PC1 vs PC2)
pca_plot_pc1_pc2 <- ggplot(pca_values, aes(x = PC1, y = PC2, color = basin, shape = species)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(title = "PCA for Fish Samples from Lake Erie (PC1 vs PC2)",
       x = "Principal Component 1", y = "Principal Component 2") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Eastern" = "#233d4d", 
                                "East Central" = "#db3a34", 
                                "West Central" = "#fcca46", 
                                "Western" = "#619b8a")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Yellow Perch" = 8,  # Stars
                                 "Walleye" = 16,     # Dots
                                 "Freshwater Drum" = 18, # Diamonds
                                 "Gizzard Shad" = 15))  # Squares

pca_plot_pc1_pc2

# Save the first plot as a PNG file in the figures folder
ggsave(here("figures", "PCA_PC1_vs_PC2_HPACs.png"), plot = pca_plot_pc1_pc2, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)

  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Yellow Perch" = 8,  # Stars
                                 "Walleye" = 16,     # Dots
                                 "Freshwater Drum" = 18, # Diamonds
                                 "Gizzard Shad" = 15))  # Squares
pca_plot_pc1_pc3

# Save the first plot as a PNG file in the figures folder
ggsave(here("figures", "PCA_PC1_vs_PC3_HPACs.png"), plot = pca_plot_pc1_pc3, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
# Create PCA biplot with dots for samples
pca_biplot <- fviz_pca_biplot(
  pca_results, 
  repel = TRUE,               # Avoid overlapping labels
  label = "var",              # Label only variables (analytes)
 
  geom.ind = "point",         # Show only dots for samples
  palette = "Dark2",          # Use a distinct color palette
  addEllipses = TRUE,         # Add confidence ellipses
  col.var = "blue",            # Variables (analytes) in red
  pointsize = 3               # Adjust point size
) +
  theme_minimal()+
   theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"), # Bold axis labels
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", size = 0.5),  # Add axis lines
    axis.text = element_text(color = "black", face = "bold"),
    plot.title = element_blank(), # Remove title
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )+  scale_color_manual(values = c("Eastern" = "#233d4d", 
                                "East Central" = "#db3a34", 
                                "West Central" = "#fcca46", 
                                "Western" = "#619b8a")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Yellow Perch" = 8,  # Stars
                                 "Walleye" = 16,     # Dots
                                 "Freshwater Drum" = 18, # Diamonds
                                 "Gizzard Shad" = 15))  # Squares
pca_biplot

# Save the plot in the "figures" folder inside the project directory
ggsave(
  filename = here("figures", "PCA_Biplot.png"), # Save as PNG in the correct folder
  plot = pca_biplot, 
  width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300
)
```

## UMAP

```{r}
set.seed(2)
# UMAP parameters
umap_config <- umap.defaults
umap_config$n_neighbors <- 10
umap_config$n_components <- 3
umap_config$min_dist <- 0.001

# Perform UMAP on the filtered concentration data
concentration_filtered1 <- concentration_filtered %>%
  select(-sample, -species, -basin)

umap_results <- umap(concentration_filtered1, config = umap_config)
umap_values <- as.data.frame(umap_results$layout)
colnames(umap_values) <- c("Variable1", "Variable2", "Variable3")
umap_values <- cbind(concentration_filtered[, c("sample", "species", "basin")], umap_values)



# Save umap_values in the output folder
write.csv(umap_values, here("output", "UMAP_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

```
